impact.headline: The first real picture of ration over-collection in Kuwait.
impact.lede: Since 1972 every Kuwaiti family has collected a monthly ration. Nobody has measured how much of it is actually used. Tamweeni households are changing that, one receipt at a time.
impact.statsCaption: Live from Tamweeni households. Updated as receipts are scanned.

governorate.title: By governorate
governorate.caption: Over-collection per governorate appears once at least 30 households report in each.
governorate.chartLabel: Over-collection rate per governorate, highest first

method.title: How the numbers are computed
method.body: Entitlement is the official per-person quota × registered household members, priced at the subsidised rate. Collected comes from scanned branch receipts. Used comes from weekly pantry check-ins. Over-collection = Σ (collected − used) ÷ Σ collected over the last three months, across households with at least one pantry check-in. No names, card numbers or addresses leave the phone.
method.request: Detailed data available on request to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
method.principle: Tamweeni never encourages taking more than a family needs; "not taken" is measured against the official entitlement.

impact.foodBankLine: Leftovers families won't use can go to the Kuwait Food Bank — optional, never a reason to take more.

source.note: Projection based on the 2025 MOCI ration figures and the pilot's first households; live numbers replace it as families join.

impact.donatedLine: + {kg} kg of leftovers given to the Kuwait Food Bank (≈ {kd})
